title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page computes an explicit presentation of a genus-1 'Teichmüller' group with two marked points, built as an extension of an extended (reflection-including) modular group by the fundamental group of the once-punctured torus.

(1) Data. u, v are free generators of pi_1 of the once-punctured torus E-{0}, a free group F_2. The loop around the puncture is l'_0, with [u,v] = l'_0^{-1}. L'_0 is the cyclic (inertia) subgroup it generates.

(2) Lifted modular elements. rho and sigma are lifts of the order-3 and order-2 generators of PSL(2,Z), and omega_0 is a 'square root' of the puncture loop: rho^3 = omega_0, sigma^2 = omega_0^{-1}, omega_0^2 = l'_0. So rho^3 sigma^2 = 1. The orientation-preserving group <rho, sigma> is the braid group B_3 (the relation is rho^3 = (sigma^{-1})^2). B_3 is the central extension of SL(2,Z) that is the mapping class group of a torus with one boundary circle; the boundary twist rho^6 is identified with l'_0.

(3) Reflections. An involution r_0 inverts rho and sigma, hence omega_0. Grothendieck then defines r_1 = r_0 rho and r_inf = sigma r_0. This gives a lifted (2,3,inf) reflection-triangle presentation (boxed): r_0^2 = r_1^2 = r_inf^2 = 1 and (r_0 r_1)^3 (r_inf r_0)^2 = 1. Its image modulo the centre is the Coxeter presentation of PGL(2,Z), and the group itself is his 'GL(2,Z)~'. The NB defines eps_0 = sigma rho, so that (sigma rho)^{-1} = r_1 r_inf.

(4) Action on F_2 (Birman-type exact sequence).
- r_0: u <-> v.
- r_inf: u -> u^{-1}, v -> u v u^{-1}.
- r_1: u -> u^{-1}, v -> u v.
- Hence rho = r_0 r_1: u -> v^{-1}, v -> v u.
- Hence sigma = r_inf r_0: u -> u v u^{-1}, v -> u^{-1}.

(5) Result. The total group is presented on generators r_0, r_1, r_inf, (omega_0,) u, v. The relations are the triangle relations, the identification of omega_0^2 with the puncture loop, and the conjugation relations (C).

(6) Identifications claimed.
- The total group (script G~_{1,1}) is isomorphic to T_{1,2}. Modulo orientation conventions, this is the (extended) mapping class group of the torus with two marked points, i.e. pi_1 of M_{1,2} = the universal punctured elliptic curve over M_{1,1}.
- The subgroup generated by the reflections, T~_{1,1} = GL(2,Z)~, is the normalizer of the inertia subgroup L'_0. This is right because a primitive commutator generates a malnormal cyclic subgroup of F_2, so the normalizer meets F_2 only in L'_0.
- The normalizer of the puncture inertia group is thus the 'tangential base point' modular group (B_3, extended by reflections).
errors: Sign inconsistency in the two final presentations. From the boxed relation rho^3 sigma^2 = 1 (which I verified on the action: rho^3 = inn(vu) composed with iota and sigma^2 = inn(uv) composed with iota, where iota is the elliptic involution, so rho^3 sigma^2 acts trivially), one gets rho^6 = sigma^{-4}. The action gives sigma^4 = inn([u,v]) and rho^6 = inn([v,u]) = inn(l'_0). So '(r_0 r_1)^6 (= (r_inf r_0)^4) = [u,v]' is wrong for the first term: it should be (r_inf r_0)^4 = [u,v] = (r_0 r_1)^{-6}.

Likewise, the last presentation '(r_0 r_1)^3 = (r_inf r_0)^2 = omega_0, omega_0^2 = [u,v]' contradicts both the boxed relation and the opening data (rho^3 = omega_0, sigma^2 = omega_0^{-1}, omega_0^2 = l'_0 = [u,v]^{-1}). It should read (r_0 r_1)^3 = (r_inf r_0)^{-2} = omega_0 with omega_0^2 = [u,v]^{-1}, or equivalently with signs adjusted.

The marginal implication next to the r_inf lines reads 'r_1(l'_0) = l'_0' (as transcribed). But r_inf([u,v]) = [u^{-1}, u v u^{-1}] = [v,u] = [u,v]^{-1}. All three reflections invert l'_0, as they must, being orientation-reversing. Either the mark is cut off at the page edge or it is a slip; it should be r_inf(l'_0) = l'_0^{-1}.
The NB 'r_inf r_inf = (sigma rho)^{-1}' must be r_1 r_inf, since sigma rho = r_inf r_1.

ideas.what: Presentation of pi_1(M_{1,2}) as an extension of the (extended) genus-1 modular group by pi_1 of the once-punctured torus, with explicit outer action on F_2
ideas.modern_name: Birman exact sequence / mapping class group of the twice-punctured torus; pi_1 of the universal elliptic curve minus origin
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birman (1969); standard in mapping class group theory; arithmetic version: Ihara, Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto
ideas.where_published: The genus-1 Teichmüller tower with T_{1,1}, T_{1,2} is mentioned in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) but without this presentation

ideas.what: Square root omega_0 of the puncture loop; orientation-preserving part <rho,sigma> = B_3 as central extension of SL(2,Z), identifying the boundary twist with the puncture loop
ideas.modern_name: B_3 = mapping class group of the torus with one boundary component; tangential base point at the cusp
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Artin, Birman); arithmetic use by Nakamura, Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps, Hain–Matsumoto

ideas.what: Normalizer of the inertia subgroup L'_0 in T_{1,2} equals the lifted modular group GL(2,Z)~
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition group of the puncture / malnormality of the boundary cyclic subgroup
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; arithmetic analogues by Nakamura ('decomposition groups at infinity')

ideas.what: Reflection-generator (Coxeter-style, (2,3,inf) triangle) presentation r_0, r_1, r_inf of the extended (orientation-reversing included) modular group, lifted to the central extension and to the surface-group extension
ideas.modern_name: Extended mapping class group presentation; PGL(2,Z) as the (2,3,inf) reflection triangle group
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical for PGL(2,Z); extended mapping class group presentations: various (e.g. Korkmaz and others)

missed.claim: Grothendieck systematically includes antiholomorphic (reflection) generators r_0, r_1, r_inf in the genus-1 Teichmüller groups. He realizes the cusp-normalizer as a lifted (2,3,inf) reflection group acting on F_2 by explicit automorphisms. This 'real structure' viewpoint (complex conjugation inside the Teichmüller tower) is little developed in the later GT/Teichmüller-tower literature, though the mathematics itself is standard.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal: complex conjugation/real points in Teichmüller towers and GT actions are a minor topic; this is only a documented early explicit computation.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard computation: a Birman-type presentation of the (extended) mapping class group of the twice-punctured torus via B_3 and reflections, with some sign slips. It documents Grothendieck's 1981 genus-1 Teichmüller-tower work, but contains nothing absent from the later literature.
transcription_corrections: 'rho^3 = omega_0^4' should be rho^3 = omega_0; the mark after omega_0 is a smudge/asterisk, not an exponent 4. This is consistent with sigma^2 = omega_0^{-1} and the boxed relation.
'Gamma~_{1,1}' is a script/Gothic G~_{1,1} in the image, not Gamma.
In the NB, 'r_inf r_inf' should be 'r_1 r_inf' (first factor overwritten).
The right-margin implication beside the r_inf lines reads 'r_1(l'_0) = l'_0' but mathematically concerns r_inf, and should give l'_0^{-1}; possibly cut off at the page edge.
'v^4[v^{-1},u]' in the r_inf(v) line is part of a crossed-out attempt, not a retained formula.
The page number written at bottom left is 131.
